prompts: Read {WS}/FACTSHEET.md: the facts about Piet Mondrian's painting "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930) and the De Stijl movement. Create {WS}/landing/index.html: a single-file landing page (HTML + inline CSS; Google Fonts allowed; no frameworks) telling its story, with art direction inspired by Piet Mondrian (asymmetric grid of rectangles, thick black lines, red, blue, yellow and white). Include a page title, a hero, sections with the key facts (the painter, the year, the movement and its principles, why the work matters), a call-to-action button and a link to the source URL given in the fact sheet. This is your ONLY request: there will be no second turn and no answers to questions. Deliver the complete, working final file. Work only inside {WS}.
answers:
[goal] Single-file Mondrian-style landing page from FACTSHEET.md.

[action] I wrote `landing/index.html` with inline CSS and Google Fonts (Archivo Black, Work Sans). It uses no frameworks. I did not open it in a browser.

[result]
- **Layout:** The page is an asymmetric CSS grid. Its 10px black gaps act as the thick lines, and the cells are red, blue, yellow and white.
- **Hero:** It shows the title, "1930" and a "Explore the painting" button that jumps to the painting section.
- **Facts:** One section covers the painter (Mondrian, 1872-1944), the year, the medium and the collection (Kunsthaus Zurich). It also covers De Stijl (founded 1917 by van Doesburg and Mondrian).
- **Principles:** A separate section lists the three Neoplasticism rules: only horizontal and vertical lines, the three primaries, and white, grey and black.
- **The picture:** A simplified CSS sketch shows the large red square at top right, the small blue square at bottom left and the small yellow rectangle at bottom right. A caption says it is a sketch and not a reproduction.
- **Why it matters:** A section states that the asymmetric balance of a few primary-colour blocks became a reference for modern graphic design and architecture.
- **Source and call to action:** The closing section has a "Read on Wikipedia" button and a text link. Both go to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composition_with_Red,_Blue_and_Yellow.
- **Extras:** The page has a mobile breakpoint, focus outlines and `prefers-reduced-motion` support.
- **Facts:** Every fact on the page comes from the fact sheet. The only added wording is the tagline "Fewer lines. Fewer colours. More balance." and the framing around it.

[next] None. Open `landing/index.html` in a browser to review it.
